question: Where does home health care primarily take place?
explanation: Home health care brings medical and nursing services directly into the patient's home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is home health care usually started after a hospital stay?

options.A: To bridge the gap between discharge and full independence
options.B: To replace long-term institutional nursing homes completely
options.C: To eliminate the need for any follow-up doctor visits
options.D: To reduce the total number of required diagnostic tests

explanation: Home care supports patients after hospital discharge, helping them safely transition back to daily life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: What is a major advantage of receiving care outside of a hospital?
explanation: Staying out of institutional facilities helps protect patients from catching hospital-borne infections. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: How does home care affect a patient's daily routine compared to a hospital stay?

options.A: Patients must wake up strictly at hospital meal times
options.B: Care is tailored around the patient's personal schedule
options.C: Nursing staff rotate shifts every single four hours
options.D: Visiting hours are heavily restricted by facility rules

explanation: Home health nurses adapt their care plans to fit nicely into the patient's normal household routine. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is a key financial benefit of home health care compared to staying in a hospital?

options.A: Government waiver of all transport fuel taxes
options.B: Complete elimination of nursing salary expenses
options.C: Reduction in expensive daily hospital room fees
options.D: Free prescription medications for all chronic diseases

explanation: Avoiding overnight hospital bed stays removes the highest daily cost in modern healthcare. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: How do home visits help save money on healthcare costs?

options.A: By shortening the recovery time of acute surgical wounds by half
options.B: By catching early warning signs before emergency admission is required
options.C: By forcing patients to purchase cheaper generic drug brands
options.D: By providing free diagnostic lab equipment to every household

explanation: Regular nursing checks at home spot health problems early, preventing costly emergency room visits. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: What can a nurse learn better during a home visit compared to a clinic consultation?

options.A: A sterile environment free from household dust
options.B: Seeing the patient's true living conditions and daily habits
options.C: Immediate backup from specialized surgical consultants
options.D: Access to high-powered laboratory diagnostic machines

explanation: Visiting the home uncovers lifestyle habits, home risks, and family support systems that clinics cannot show. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why does home care often improve the mental well-being of chronically ill patients?

options.A: It guarantees complete recovery from all progressive neurological diseases
options.B: It prevents family members from ever visiting or interfering
options.C: It removes the need to take any daily oral medications
options.D: It preserves personal autonomy and reduces feelings of institutionalization

explanation: Staying in familiar surroundings gives patients a sense of control and prevents hospital-related depression. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is a major limitation of home health care?

options.A: Lack of qualified nurses willing to travel to private homes
options.B: Inability to replicate intensive hospital monitoring for unstable patients
options.C: Prohibition of oral medication administration outside clinics
options.D: Mandatory requirement for patients to own an ambulance

explanation: Patients who need continuous, high-level life support require specialized hospital units rather than home care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is a common supply challenge when treating patients in residential settings?

options.A: Mandatory legal liability for neighborhood environmental noise
options.B: Automatic rejection of insurance claims by government agencies
options.C: Immediate loss of electricity during every single nursing shift
options.D: Supply shortages due to the absence of central hospital stores

explanation: Private homes do not keep hospital supplies stocked, so missing items can sometimes delay care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which physical hazard is a nurse most likely to face in a patient's home?

options.A: Industrial chemical spills on living room floors
options.B: High-voltage electrical surgical equipment in the kitchen
options.C: Industrial radiation leaks from household appliances
options.D: Low domestic beds that cause back strain during procedures

explanation: Normal house beds do not adjust in height like hospital beds, which can cause back pain for nurses. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: How do home environments differ from hospital wards regarding safety for nurses?

options.A: Private homes feature mandatory ergonomic equipment standards
options.B: Home environments are largely uncontrolled and unpredictable
options.C: Infections are strictly nonexistent in community settings
options.D: Hospitals lack security personnel found in residential areas

explanation: When working in private homes, nurses encounter unpredictable factors like pets and poor lighting. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why is keeping patient information private harder during home visits?

options.A: Family members and neighbors are often present in the home
options.B: Patient diagnoses are broadcast on local radio stations
options.C: Community nurses are legally required to publish treatment notes
options.D: Medical records must be displayed publicly on household walls

explanation: The open layout of a home makes it harder to keep medical discussions away from family members and visitors. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h7)

question: What ethical challenge happens when a clear-headed patient refuses home care advice?

options.A: Balancing respect for patient autonomy with the duty to prevent harm
options.B: Deciding whether to bill the family for uncompleted nursing tasks
options.C: Reporting the patient to the police for illegal drug possession
options.D: Forcing compliance by withholding all prescribed pain relief

explanation: Nurses must weigh the patient's right to make choices against the need to keep them safe. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is a good way to protect nurses from dangers before starting home care?

options.A: Insisting that all nursing procedures be performed outdoors
options.B: Sending two police officers on every single routine home visit
options.C: Requiring the patient to move to a new apartment building
options.D: Conducting a thorough safety assessment prior to the first visit

explanation: Checking for risks beforehand helps agencies put proper safety measures in place for staff. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h8)

question: Why are regular team meetings important in home health care?

options.A: To reduce the financial salaries of participating health workers
options.B: To eliminate all regulatory nursing documentation requirements
options.C: To replace the need for physical home visits with virtual meetings
options.D: To ensure doctors, nurses, and therapists share unified treatment goals

explanation: Teamwork among healthcare workers stops conflicting instructions and makes patient care safer. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h8)
